channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
item.description: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.

item.title: [ECFR] After Putin’s photo op, Europe must rejoin great-power diplomacy
item.description: The Shenzhen summit gave Putin recognition as an equal in a US-China-Russia format. But Europe should not mistake a vague declaration for a breakthrough, and it should insist on a seat at the diplomatic table

item.title: [ECFR] Cleaner together: Why energy cooperation is vital for a fossil-free Europe
item.description: Europe remains dependent on fossil fuels and has no clear phase-out goal. The EU’s six biggest states should unite through regional forums to lead Europe’s energy transition

item.title: [DW] Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

item.title: [DW] EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
item.description: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

item.title: [ECFR] Networked nationalism: The global ambitions of Spain’s Vox party
item.description: Other Europeans should assume the far-right party would wield considerable foreign-policy influence in any Spanish government it joins

item.title: [ECFR] COP31 failed, but the green transition has not
item.description: COP31 ended without an overarching agreement, but Europe can still be a leader in the global green transition

item.title: [EU Observer] EU leaders leave Brussels with no budget deal, piling pressure on Christmas summit
item.description: The so-called 'frugal' EU states want deeper cuts, the 'Friends of Cohesion' group wants agriculture and regional funding spared, and Antonio Costa's €204bn compromise satisfies no one.

item.title: [EU Observer] A ‘bad’ summit first, an EU budget deal later
item.description: Everyone at the summit insists their red lines are unbreakable — yet the real story is how far they will bend once the ticking clock, Ukraine’s bills and looming 2027 elections start to crush their resolve.

item.title: [DW] Albania's youth are protesting, no longer leaving the country
item.description: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

item.title: [EU Observer] Spain’s Hernández de Cos tapped to succeed fellow ‘owl’ Lagarde as ECB president
item.description: Neither dove nor hawk, the former Bank of Spain governor describes himself as an 'owl' when it comes to monetary policy, just like his predecessor Christine Lagarde did when she took over the helm in 2019.

item.title: [DW] FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
item.description: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

item.title: [EU Observer] Mass-produced, small, and cheap Russian missiles could shape the war in 2027, making Ukrainian cities into constant targets (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,736)
item.description: A massive ramp-up in low-cost Russian missiles risks turning Ukrainian cities, power plants, and factories into constant targets, just as Kyiv struggles to finance interceptors and its own long‑range weapons.

item.title: [EU Observer] Magyar shows what Hungary’s new policy on Ukraine could look like (Day 198 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Péter Magyar plays volleyball with Volodymyr Zelensky, but vows no blank cheque for Kyiv. He is simultaneously hitting Hungary’s oligarchs with a new wealth tax, sidelining Orbán loyalists from sports and culture, and watching Fidesz-friendly pollsters admit his party is now well ahead.

item.title: [DW] Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
item.description: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

item.title: [DW] Russia-Ukraine war extends to Baltic, Mediterranean
item.description: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Ukraine is trying to increase the pressure on Russia and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?

item.title: [DW] Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
item.description: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Spanish PM candidate Feijóo visits Ceuta during election blackout day
item.description: The center-right front-runner said he was "fulfilling a personal commitment" to the enclave and its mayor on a day when campaigning is forbidden.

item.title: [Euractiv] Google halts construction of Belgian data centre on authorities’ order
item.description: A row over water use has dogged the project amid local drought fears.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Greek junior minister resigns amid public contracts controversy
item.description: Vangelis Liakos was put in post two weeks ago after another scandal led to a minister resigning from Kyriakos Mitsotakis's government.

item.title: [DW] Azerbaijan's opposition leader Ali Karimli: A year behind bars
item.description: Azerbaijani opposition leader Ali Karimli has been in prison since November 2025. Authorities accuse him of attempting to seize power by force, but human rights groups say his prosecution is politically motivated.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine's expertise comes in handy for international drone alliances
item.description: Ukrainian expertise merged with Europe's financial and industrial clout: Germany and other countries are expanding drone partnerships with Ukraine and reshaping Europe's defense industry in the process.

item.title: [Financial Times] The outsider from Cannes shaking up France’s presidential race
item.description: Rightwing mayor David Lisnard has surged in polls with punchy attacks on the bloated state and promises of radical spending cuts

item.title: [DW] As Spain votes, what could change for Europe?
item.description: Spain votes on Sunday. A loss for Pedro Sanchez and a shift to the right in Madrid could affect how one of the EU's largest countries approaches migration, defense and the war in Gaza.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Santiago Abascal: Spain’s far-right kingmaker
item.description: The man who built Vox into Spain’s most successful far-right force now faces his biggest test: translating electoral gains into a lasting role in government.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Putin’s latest wonder weapon – a nuclear-armed ‘Death Star’ satellite – may be ‘sheer hysteria’, expert warns
item.description: There is no open-source evidence that Russia is about to launch a nuclear-armed satellite over the EU's head, in what sounded like Western paranoia about Vladimir Putin's supposed "wonder-weapons".

item.title: [EU Observer] Czech Republic used to be one of the EU’s most fiscally conservative hawks, now it demands more cash
item.description: Through his ultimatums for a higher EU budget, Czech prime minister Andrej Babiš has manufactured ammunition for his anti-EU political allies across the continent. Europe will remember Czech Republic for its self-centred, arrogant and cunning approach to EU long-term budget negotiations

item.description: A People's Party-Vox coalition of the centre-right and far-right will reshape Madrid’s stance on migration, Israel, and climate policy, while shifting Spain closer to Europe’s increasingly rightwing political mainstream.

item.title: [DW] Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
item.description: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.

item.description: Influencers can sell a glamorised lifestyle without it looking like an ad, and consumers are fooled. Though airlines get the win, the effects of over-tourism, climate deterioration, and basic legal transparency are increasingly difficult to ignore.

item.description: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

item.description: Mohannad Rajab (مهند رجب), born c. 1979, is a member of Hamas’s Military Council and commander of the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades in Gaza City. He was previously a member of the group’s intelligence division. According to Israeli sources, he took over as head of the Qassam Brigades following Israel’s assassination of Ezz al-Din Hadad […]

item.description: Ali al-Amoudi (علي العمودي), born in Khan Younis in 1975, is a veteran member of Hamas’s armed wing, the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades. Amoudi was considered close to the group’s former Gaza leader, Yahya Sinwar, who he met while in prison, and became his chief of staff in 2017. Amoudi was member ‘Unit Zero’ — […]

item.title: [ECFR] Nafiz Sobaih
item.description: Nafiz Sobaih (نافذ صبيح) has been a member of Hamas’s Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades since the 1990s. He is currently the commander of the group’s Military Oversight Authority which is tasked with counter-espionage and internal discipline. Sobaih survived an Israeli assassination attempt targeting him in Gaza City in August 2026.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why isn’t European TV drama responding to the threat of war?
item.description: The possibility of nuclear war in Europe is openly discussed. Studios and broadcasters can treat these threats as too bleak, too political, or too hard to sell. Or they can recognise that loyalty, power, fear, and responsibility to our children are the oldest dramatic subjects, and that they have never mattered more.
